question.text: Two identical spheres each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> are fixed at the ends of a light rod so that the separation between the centers is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>150</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. Then, moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through its middle point is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>20</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, where the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Using parallel axis theorem, we can write total moment of inertia as, I=25mR2+md2×2

⇒I=225×2×122+2×342=5320 kg m2

Therefore, x=53.
